evidence.quote: And so one big piece of performance for a given harness is what, what is your like rate of, of token caching?
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

evidence.quote: And so the harness will do some sort of, you know, summarization, compression, compaction, whatever you want to call it.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

evidence.quote: How often will your harness preserve that through compaction?

evidence.quote: Naively, everyone believed initially was if you train the model and you build the harness, you're going to make them better together.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

evidence.quote: If you build a harness that supports different models, that harness will be better.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

evidence.quote: Which is why, like, and this is something that, you know, I think was somewhat frustrating to, because ideally, like from a lab perspective, you ideally want it so that it's better together, because then that means you have to use their harness and you can't use a different one.
